vault.title: Lab 01 - Image basics (numpy)
vault.summary: This document outlines the first laboratory assignment for an Introduction to Computer Vision course. Students will learn how to treat images as numpy arrays by performing basic operations like building an RGB gradient image, converting it to grayscale, cropping and flipping regions, computing intensity histograms, and thresholding. The deliverable is a Jupyter notebook named lab01.ipynb containing code cells for each of the five tasks.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, lab sessions, and grading policy for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn core computer vision topics ranging from image filtering and edge detection to deep learning and object detection. The course grade is composed of 30 percent labs, 30 percent midterm, and 40 percent final project.
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in image filtering
Canny: A popular edge detection operator
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform for local feature extraction
Homography: A transformation relating the planes of two images
RANSAC: Random Sample Consensus algorithm for robust fitting
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network used for image classification and vision tasks

vault.title: Lecture 01: Introduction
vault.summary: This introductory lecture for Introduction to Computer Vision covers the basic course structure, grading policy, and foundational concepts. Students learn how digital images are represented as multidimensional arrays defined by height, width, and channels with uint8 data types. The session also introduces essential Python libraries used throughout the course, including numpy, OpenCV, and matplotlib.
key_terms: Image arrays: Digital images represented as matrices with height, width, and channels.
dtype uint8: Unsigned 8-bit integer data type commonly used for pixel values.
numpy: A Python library for numerical computing and array manipulation.
OpenCV: A library specialized in computer vision tasks.
matplotlib: A plotting library used for data visualization.
